covers: US October CPI, the Wall Street open and the JSE close, Tuesday 10 November 2026
headline: Hotter-than-expected US inflation lifts the 10-year Treasury yield to 4.98%; Wall Street opens lower and the rand weakens to R16.50/$
summary: The JSE All Share closed at 114,551.87, down 0.4% on the day, and the rand weakened to R16.50/$ from R16.37/$ at 11:41 SAST (Yahoo Finance, 10 Nov). US October consumer prices rose more than expected (CNBC headline, 10 Nov), the US 10-year Treasury yield jumped to 4.98% from 4.86% on Monday, and early in the session the S&P 500 was at 7,523.54 (-0.3%) and the Nasdaq at 25,188.22 (-0.3%) (Yahoo Finance, 10 Nov 16:58 SAST). Gold slipped to $4,046.50 and Brent held near $90.23 (Yahoo Finance, 10 Nov), so higher US rates are now the main pressure on the rand and on gold miners.

items.title: US October CPI rises more than expected; markets weigh a bigger Fed hike in December
items.summary: CNBC reports that October consumer prices rose more than economists expected, complicating the Fed's fight against inflation, and MarketWatch reports Fed Governor Waller has put a half-point hike into the mix for December (headlines, 10 Nov 2026). The Fed funds target is 3.75%–4.00% after the 28 October hold (StockAnalysis, 28 Oct). Detailed CPI figures will be added once checked against the BLS release.

items.title: US 10-year Treasury yield jumps to 4.98% from 4.86%
items.summary: The yield rose about 12 basis points from Monday's close after the inflation data (Yahoo Finance ^TNX, 10 Nov 2026 16:58 SAST vs 9 Nov close). Higher US yields usually weigh on emerging-market currencies such as the rand and on non-yielding gold.
items.source: Yahoo Finance via LRC Market Dashboard, 10 Nov 2026 16:58 SAST
